title: Multi-Agent Environment with Virtual Sequences
description: Milestone M5: wire a configuration agent, a data-in agent and a passive data-out agent into one environment, order configuration before data and reconfigure at a safe point with a virtual sequence, check end to end with a scoreboard that follows the configuration bus by time stamp, add cross-interface ordering assertions, and prove that three mutant tests and two planted DUT bugs all fail.
outcome: Wire three agents into one bench and order configuration before data with a virtual sequence.

steps.title: Step 1: Read the specification and run the starter
steps.instructions: Read the key_stream specification in the README (rules R1 to R4) and the complete parts of work/mx_tb.sv: the three interfaces, the agents, the agent sequences and mx_reconfig_test. Build work/key_stream.sv with work/mx_tb.sv and run it. It stops at 0 ns with UVM_FATAL [NO_CFG] from uvm_test_top.env.cfg_agt. Before you open the README's answer, say which component failed to do its job.

steps.title: Step 2: The topology: per-agent configuration and the virtual sequencer
steps.instructions: In mx_env::build_phase, set each agent's configuration object at its own path (cfg_agt, din_agt, dout_agt; field name cfg) before the agents are created. In connect_phase, copy cfg_agt.sqr and din_agt.sqr into vsqr, and connect cfg_agt.ap, din_agt.ap and dout_agt.ap to the scoreboard's cfg_imp, in_imp and out_imp. Rerun: the run now ends with SCB_SUMMARY matches=0 mismatches=0 pending=0 order=0 and RESULT TEST PASSED. Answer the README's question: is it a pass?

steps.title: Step 3: The virtual sequence decides the order
steps.instructions: In mx_reconfig_vseq, fill in check_handles (a named UVM_FATAL NO_SQR for each null handle in p_sequencer) and body: check the handles, program_dut(KEY_1, MODE_XOR), send_burst(FIRST_1, BURST_LEN), program_dut(KEY_2, MODE_ADD), send_burst(FIRST_2, BURST_LEN), each one after the other. Explain why the second program_dut call is a safe point.

steps.title: Step 4: The end-to-end scoreboard follows the configuration bus
steps.instructions: Fill in mx_scoreboard from the specification: apply (R1 and R4 on the shadow registers, ORDER for a KEY write while en is 1), commit_before (apply every pending write stamped earlier than t), predict (R3), write_cfg, write_in (ORDER for a byte sent while en is 0, otherwise push the prediction), write_out (compare with !==) and check_phase (SCB_PENDING, SCB_NO_TRAFFIC). Run mx_reconfig_test and expect SCB_SUMMARY matches=12 mismatches=0 pending=0 order=0.

steps.title: Step 5: Cross-interface ordering assertions
steps.instructions: In tb_top, add ORDER_SVA (din_bus.valid implies dut.en) and LOCK_SVA (a KEY write on cfg_bus implies !dut.en), clocked on posedge clk, disabled while rst_n is 0, each reporting with `uvm_error in its action block. Rerun mx_reconfig_test: the log must still end with RESULT TEST PASSED, UVM_ERROR : 0 and UVM_FATAL : 0.

steps.title: Step 6: Run the mutant tests
steps.instructions: Without editing work/mx_mutants.svh, run +UVM_TESTNAME=mx_data_first_test, mx_no_quiesce_test and mx_passive_cfg_test. Predict each signature before you run it, then compare with the README's table: 3 ORDER and 3 ORDER_SVA with matches=9; 1 ORDER and 1 LOCK_SVA with matches=12; UVM_FATAL [NO_SQR] at 0 ns. Every mutant must end with RESULT TEST FAILED or a fatal.

steps.title: Step 7: Break the DUT and watch the bench catch it
steps.instructions: Run mx_reconfig_test with +BUG=1 (MODE ignored) and with +BUG=2 (EN takes effect one edge late), and compare each summary with the README's table. Then plant your own bug in work/key_stream.sv: make a CTRL write while EN is 1 also update MODE. Predict which test catches it, run all four tests, then remove it and rerun mx_reconfig_test: RESULT TEST PASSED.
